subject: GeoSplit standby switchover acceptance & test criteria
messages:

To: Sato Takahashi <sato@zenhealth.jp>, Maya Patel <maya.p@zenhealth.jp>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: GeoSplit standby switchover acceptance & test criteria

Hi Sato / Maya —

Thanks for the call yesterday. Per ZenHealth’s residency requirements and our recent private-deploy topology conversation, attached is the proposed acceptance checklist for the GeoSplit standby switchover (EU primary, APAC warm-standby). High-level asks:

- Confirmation that the proposed blackout window (2 hours) on Saturday 2027-07-03 is acceptable.
- Approval of the acceptance criteria below so we can schedule a cutover dry-run:
  1) Traffic drain from EU to APAC: verified zero customer PII egress to non-EU subnets during switchover.
  2) KMS usage: keys for EU tenant remain in EU KMS; no cross-region key export.
  3) DNS & routing: failover via BGP+DNS with 30s DNS TTL; validation of geo-routing enforcement.
  4) Recovery time objective (RTO) target: < 5 minutes for inference path failover (observed at model-entry).
  5) Auditability: post-cutover logs showing request origin, model shard location, and keystore access records.

Attached: geosplit-test-plan.pdf (step-by-step runbook) and network-diagram.vsdx (edge/VPC peering view). Karthik, I’ve pasted a few open questions for infra below — can you confirm that these are achievable without a temporary deviation from the residency policy?

Open questions (for Redwood infra):
- During the switchover we plan to warm cache on APAC to avoid cold-start amplification; will KV cache pre-population write any customer metadata to APAC storage?
- If a control-plane fallback is required, does the control plane pass any PII in logs to a US-based aggregator?

Sato / Maya: if the acceptance items look good, please reply with any procurement or legal gating items (DocuSign, export control forms) and we’ll lock the date.

Ben

Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 22:06:00 +09:00
Subject: Re: GeoSplit standby switchover acceptance & test criteria

Ben —

Thanks for the clear checklist. High level: ZenHealth is comfortable with a 2-hour window for a dry-run as long as the following are explicitly validated in the runbook:

- All cryptographic material (keys/certs) for EU tenants must remain provisioned and used within EU KMS for the duration of the test. Any temporary usage outside EU must be pre-authorized and logged.
- No persistent storage of patient-identifiable fields in APAC zone during or after the test; ephemeral caching for inference is OK if not written to durable storage.
- We need a signed attestation from Redwood Ops that the control-plane telemetry samples do not contain PII and that log retention for this run will follow ZenHealth retention (30 days).

I can confirm procurement is aligned to start the DocuSign exchange — Maya will send the PO/contacts. Please add a short checklist item for the attestation wording (we can provide a template).

—Sato
Sato Takahashi
Head of Infrastructure, ZenHealth
sato@zenhealth.jp
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 6 Jun 2027 02:33:00 +05:30
Subject: Re: GeoSplit standby switchover acceptance & test criteria

Ben / Sato —

Quick answers and technical confirmation from infra:

- KV cache pre-population: design is purely in-memory on the serving nodes in APAC. We have a strict NODUR policy for the warm cache path: nothing is written to persistent disk or to object storage. I’ll attach the keystore-residency-matrix.xlsx showing where secrets are used.

- KMS behavior: EU tenant keys will remain in the EU KMS. The runtime will call the EU KMS endpoint over a secure peering link; no key material is exported. Access logs are available and we can snapshot them for the attestation.

- Control-plane telemetry: our control-plane sampling pipeline scrubs PII by default; however, for auditors we can run a redacted pipeline and provide a signed statement from Security.

Operational notes for the runbook (from network team):
- Failover mechanism: primary method is BGP withdrawal from EU to force immediate egress change; secondary method is DNS failover with 30s TTL. We will test both in sequence during the dry-run (primary only for the first test).
- RTO measurement: synthetic traffic will be injected at the model entry tier and measured via the tracing hooks in Redwood Console. Target is 3–4 minutes observed median.

Attachments: geosplit-test-plan.pdf (v1.2), network-diagram.vsdx, keystore-residency-matrix.xlsx

I will be available during the window for runbook execution. If ZenHealth wants us to run the first dry-run in a staged manner (subset of traffic -> full switch), we can do that.

Karthik

Thanks — that all looks good from procurement and legal. Two quick items before we sign off:

1) Can Redwood provide the attestation PDF (signed) and the KMS access-log snapshot on the day of the dry-run? We will attach both to the PO.
2) Please confirm the rollback plan (we prefer immediate BGP re-announce to return traffic to EU if any privacy anomaly is detected).

If those items are in the runbook we’ll countersign the DocuSign and issue the PO next week.

Best,
Maya Patel
